title: Permission Simulator: What-if access preview and bulk rollback flows for org/workspace RBAC
creator: Anya Singh
description: Design a 'Permission Simulator' in the Redwood Console that lets admins preview the impact of proposed RBAC changes (role edits, role assignments, workspace moves) across organization and workspace scope before committing them. The feature should also surface affected users and resources, show consequences in the audit log preview, and provide a safe bulk-rollback mechanism that can revert a recently applied change and create an automated recovery plan. Target flows: proposal -> impact preview -> staged apply -> commit with audit snapshot -> bulk rollback. Emphasis on clear affordances for cross-workspace role grants, inherited permissions, and temporary grants (expiry).
acceptance_criteria: Admins can create a proposed RBAC change set and run a simulator that lists all directly and transitively affected users and resources with counts and severity tags (read/write/admin).
Simulator provides a diff-style preview of changed permissions per user and per workspace, including inherited roles and temporary grants with expiry metadata.
Proposed changes can be staged and saved as a 'change package' that appears in the audit timeline as a pending entry, and can be committed or canceled.

After commit, the console records an immutable audit snapshot of the change package and exposes a one-click 'Bulk Rollback' that reverses the package and logs the rollback entry with a recovery ticket link.
Design passes accessibility review (WCAG AA) for color contrast and keyboard navigation for simulator tables and modals.

Prototype usability test with at least 6 org-admin participants achieves task completion rate >= 85% on two tasks: (1) correctly identify highest-risk affected user, (2) perform a staged rollback after a mistaken commit.
Handoff artifacts: annotated Figma prototype, specs for API surface (preview endpoint + commit/rollback webhooks), and a component inventory for Engineering.

decisions: Adopt two-phase simulation: (1) Fast estimate using cached aggregates for large orgs, (2) Full expand on user request with progress indicator.
Expose a single 'change package' object in UI to represent staged changes; change packages are first-class and appear in the audit timeline as a pending entry.
Bulk Rollback will be limited to reversing the last N change packages (configurable, default N=5) and will use the audit snapshot to compute revert actions atomically where possible.
Simulator will be accessible only to org-admin and workspace-admin roles; commit/rollback actions require MFA when the package affects >100 users or has 'high' severity.
Security requires simulated outputs to redact exact resource IDs for non-admin viewers; console will provide aggregated counts instead.
